overlap.title: Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes between Cyrus and Darius — which kings are meant, and is the order of telling the order of events?
overlap.summary: Ezra 4 tells of opposition from the days of Cyrus “until the reign of Darius”, then of an accusation under Ahasuerus and letters under Artaxerxes about the city and its walls, and then says the work on the house stopped until the second year of Darius. The verses do not say who these two kings are or whether their reigns fall before Darius.
overlap.reasoning: The answer changes what the chapter reports. If the two kings reigned between Cyrus and Darius, the letters may be read as preceding and contributing to the stoppage of 4:24; sequence alone does not establish that causal link. If they are later kings, the chapter gathers opposition from several reigns and 4:24 takes up again from 4:5; the letters then concern a later building of the city, which is what they speak of: in the KJV of Ezra 4:8–23 the words “house” and “temple” do not occur, and the letters speak of the city and its walls. The book also names an Artaxerxes after Darius among those by whose commandment the house was finished, though it dates the finishing to Darius’s sixth year.
overlap.scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. Readings that have been proposed, none of which the quoted verses state: that Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes here are names of kings who reigned between Cyrus and Darius; that they are the kings who bear those names in Esther and in Ezra 7 and Nehemiah, the passage being out of the order of time; that 4:24 resumes 4:5 after a digression. What the verses do state is the order of telling, the names, that the letters speak of the city and its walls, and that the work of the house ceased until the second year of Darius. Check made: the thirteen verses quoted were read in the KJV, and 4:6 and 4:7 in the Hebrew and in Brenton’s Greek. A whole-word search of the packaged KJV finds “Ahasuerus” at Ezra 4:6, in Esther and at Daniel 9:1, and “Artaxerxes” at Ezra 4:7; Ezra 4:8; Ezra 4:11; Ezra 4:23; Ezra 6:14; Ezra 7:1; Ezra 7:7; Ezra 7:11; Ezra 7:12; Ezra 7:21; Ezra 8:1; Nehemiah 2:1; Nehemiah 5:14; Nehemiah 13:6. That is a word search, not a reading of those books. These checked verses do not explicitly settle which kings are meant or where their reigns fall. No date from outside the Bible is used. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.
